title: dedicated: autoscaling policies, burst controls, and fleet utilization reporting
author: Arjun Rao
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while still allowing short bursts to handle traffic spikes. Current autoscaling only reacts to average utilization; it lacks a configurable burst budget and fleet-level utilization reporting for SLO tracking. This PR introduces: 1) a per-fleet autoscaling policy extension (burst_budget_ms, min_guaranteed_rps, dynamic_scale_window) so operators can carve out short-term burst capacity while preserving long-term guarantees; 2) a new burst controller in the scheduler that enforces burst budgets and gracefully throttles overflow to lower-cost model variants; 3) Prometheus metrics and internal telemetry for fleet utilization and burst consumption (redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization, redwood_dedicated_burst_consumption_ratio, redwood_dedicated_min_guaranteed_rps); 4) an admin API surface to read/update autoscale and burst configs (/admin/api/v1/fleets/{id}/autoscale) and a console metrics panel preview (console changes in a follow-up UI PR). The description below summarizes changes, tests, rollout, and monitoring.

Changes: - runtime/scheduler: add burst controller and enforcement hooks; integrate with existing autoscaler policy evaluator. - controlplane/api: extend FleetAutoscaleSpec with burst_budget_ms and min_guaranteed_rps flags. - controlplane/handlers: admin endpoints to read/update policies, backed by validation and audit logs. - telemetry: new Prometheus metric exports and a short-lived event stream for burst events for debugging. - integration-tests: add workload simulation that exercises burst budget usage and validates min_guaranteed_rps guarantees; add perf microbench to assert scheduler overhead < 2% at 10k rps. - docs: brief inline API doc and Linear ticket next steps to add console UX.

Checklist: [x] design doc in Linear ENG-4123 [x] unit tests for policy validation [x] integration test for burst use-case [x] perf microbench [x] audit logs for policy changes [x] canary rollout plan included

Testing: Unit tests added for policy schema and scheduler hooks. Integration harness simulates a fleet with sustained 2000 rps and periodic 20s bursts (+5x) to ensure burst_budget_ms consumption and subsequent enforcement while min_guaranteed_rps is preserved. CI initially failed one perf benchmark (flaky microbench) which was stabilized by increasing realistic scheduling window and rerun. Local e2e and staging canary verified behavior against a synthetic load generator.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime feature-flag dedicated_autoscale_burst_v1. Canary rollout: 1) enable in staging, run smoke and perf for 48h; 2) enable for 10% of fleets in prod (low-risk customers) for 72h; 3) expand to 50% then to all fleets. Emergency rollback: disable feature flag or set burst_budget_ms=0 to disable bursts, both are supported and audited.

Monitoring & SLOs: new dashboard panels for fleet_utilization and burst_consumption_ratio. Alerts: sustained burst_consumption_ratio > 0.9 for > 1h -> paging. Added a low-priority alert for scheduler overhead regression (>5% of CPU time).

Related: Linear ENG-4123, PM-987; SUP-821 (customer report prompting guaranteed throughput option).

Author (Arjun Rao): Changed to an atomic counters + sharded token bucket to keep hot path lock-free; perf microbench shows ~1.6% overhead at 10k rps.

Exposes new Prometheus metrics: redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization and redwood_dedicated_burst_consumption_ratio. Feature gated behind 'dedicated_autoscale_burst_v1'.
